title: Nontrivial $q$-th root of unity in $\bbf_{p^{q-1}}$
statement: Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct primes. Then the field $\bbf_{p^{q-1}}$ contains an element $\omega \neq 1$ satisfying $\omega^{q} = 1$; that is, a nontrivial $q$-th root of unity.
replaced:
If $p \neq q$ are primes, then there is $\omega \in \mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}$ with
$\omega^{q} = 1$ and $\omega \neq 1$.
